conditions.view.description.is-self: The entry is the signed-in end user's own account. It applies to the end-user type only, and it matches nothing for Public, where nobody is signed in. While a role uses it, the email and the username can't be changed by updating the entry: they change through the account endpoints, which verify the new value.
conditions.view.description.is-owner: The entry's owner is the signed-in end user: it matches when the relation to the end-user type that the role chooses (field) points at them, and it matches nothing for Public. It applies to content types that have such a relation, and a content type with only one needs no choice. When the role holds it on Create, the relation is set to the signed-in user (turn that off with setOnCreate), and on update the relation can't be changed, so an owner can't hand an entry to someone else.
